subject: Recap: Token economics & next steps — Folio pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@folio.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Token economics & next steps — Folio pilot

Liam / team —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I put a formal proposal together: 

- High-level use case: conversational assistant + summarization for customer support workflows.
- Preliminary volume band (from call): 50M — 200M tokens/month depending on staged rollouts.
- Primary outcomes you care about: predictable per-token cost, latency under 250ms p95, and auditability for finance.

What I need from you to firm up pricing:
1) Confirmation on monthly token run-rate (best to give a realistic low/expected/high).
2) Who is the economic buyer (name + email) and who will sign procurement/POs?
3) Any procurement constraints (SLA, SOC2 paperwork owner, PO terms).

Next steps: I will send a tiered pricing schedule and an initial mutual action plan (attached). If you can confirm buyer & expected monthly tokens, I can include a pilot price and committed-cap pricing in the proposal.

Attaching: Folio_MA_plan_v1.pdf (outline + milestones).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Folio_MA_plan_v1.pdf (13KB)]
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@folio.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anya Singh <anya.singh@folio.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: Token economics & next steps — Folio pilot

Thanks, Jordan — good summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Expected traffic profile (more accurate): ~5M — 10M messages/day initially. Average payload ~150 tokens => roughly 225M — 450M tokens/month depending on adoption.
- Our procurement & finance: Anya Singh (CFO) will be the economic buyer and will coordinate procurement. I'm looping her in above.
- Compliance: we need SOC2 evidence and a short security questionnaire answered before legal engages.

If you can send target $/1M tokens at the volumes above and a proposed 30-day pilot price cap, that will help speed internal approval. Also include the procurement contact info you need us to populate.

Cheers,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Product
Folio AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@folio.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Token economics & next steps — Folio pilot

Liam — appreciate the detail and for looping Anya in. Based on the 225M—450M/mo estimate, here are two options we typically present: 

Option A — Hosted, tiered (no reserve):
- 0 — 50M: $450 / 1M tokens
- 50M — 200M: $350 / 1M tokens
- 200M — 500M: $300 / 1M tokens

Option B — Dedicated (reserved capacity, monthly commit):
- Example committed level 250M/mo => effective $220 / 1M tokens (includes lower latency SLO and predictable throughput).

Pilot suggestion: 30-day hosted pilot capped at 250M tokens. We can offer a pilot rate of $320 / 1M tokens for that period to demonstrate performance and allow you to validate unit economics. If you convert to Dedicated within 60 days, we can apply credited difference toward committed capacity fees.

To proceed I need: confirmed economic buyer (Anya?), procurement contact (PO email), and SOC2 point-of-contact to push the questionnaire. 

Attaching our current pricing grid for internal visibility.

Thanks — I can turn this into a short one-page commercial proposal once you confirm buyer + procurement contact.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_pricing_schedule_v2.xlsx (22KB)]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Folio pilot economics — quick approval needed

Marissa / Priyom / Rafael —

Folio just pushed a corrected volume estimate: 225M — 450M tokens/month. They asked for a 30-day pilot capped at 250M and requested a pilot rate of $320 / 1M. They explicitly named Anya Singh (CFO) as the economic buyer and will route procurement through procure@folio.ai.

Quick ask: can we approve a pilot at $320 / 1M for up to 250M tokens (hosted) without an uplift on credits? If not, what's the floor we can accept and any required terms (cap on tokens, PO upfront, or credit holdback)?

Top-of-envelope impact at 250M tokens:
- Pilot revenue at $320 / 1M => $80k (for 250M)
- If converted to Dedicated at $220 / 1M, revenue/ARR profile improves but requires reserved commit.

I'm flagging the ask to accelerate the buyer approval — they want commercial numbers to share with finance today. Need guidance within 24 hours to avoid slowing momentum.

Thanks,
Jordan
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@folio.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anya Singh <anya.singh@folio.ai>, procure@folio.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: Token economics & next steps — Folio pilot

Jordan —

Confirming Anya is the economic buyer and she'll coordinate procurement. Anya (cc'ed) — we discussed a 30-day pilot at $320 / 1M for up to 250M tokens. Procurement (procure@folio.ai) will send PO instructions and timeline once we have the pricing and SOC2 evidence.

Can you also share the SOC2 pack or a link to the security questionnaire so we can loop legal, and confirm who will be our Redwood contact for the pilot kickoff?

Thanks — looking forward to the one-pager.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Product
Folio AI
